issue.title: just symvision red: usage_windows.py sase-telegram pragmas report 4 symbols unreferenced though telegram uses them via aliased/attribute access
issue.description:
`just symvision` (and so `just check` at lint) fails on clean master (59f5eff16) with four pragma errors in `src/sase/integrations/usage_windows.py` (lines 141, 467, 487, 517): `external repository 'https://github.com/sase-org/sase-telegram.git' does not reference symbol` for `usage_windows_report`, `resolve_usage_provider`, `request_usage_windows_refresh`, `live_usage_refresh_operations`. Added by 315746c2a (usage-windows integration facade, agent 0t6).

Yet sase-telegram origin/HEAD (00af5db, release 0.4.22) DOES use all four, but only indirectly: `src/sase_telegram/inbound_handlers/usage_command.py` lists them as string literals, imports them aliased (`usage_windows_report as _usage_report`), and calls them as `facade.usage_windows_report(...)` attribute access. Likely root cause: symvision's external-reference matcher does not count aliased imports / module-attribute access (or reads a different ref than origin/HEAD). Fix either the pragma form (e.g. a matcher-visible reference) or the matcher.

Reproduced 2026-09-27 by the sase-1b1.8 land agent twice (before and after fetching the linked sase-telegram checkout); also reported as PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP by sase-1b1.8.1 and sase-1b1.8.3. Blocks every agent's `just check` lint stage.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic: identical 4 errors on every run, on clean trees, across three agents and a fresh telegram fetch.

issue.creation_reason: Every agent's just check is red at lint on clean master; proposed by sase-1b1.8.1 and sase-1b1.8.3 and reproduced by the sase-1b1.8 land agent.

evidence.note: Independent repro by sase-1b2.land on master c78eb3805: symvision src/sase reports the 4 usage_windows.py sase-telegram pragma errors (lines 141/467/487/517) against the current telegram checkout 00af5db; telegram references the names only through a facade object in tests/test_usage_command.py. With those 4 stubbed, the only other symvision error is _segment_section_identity (sase-1b1.8.2, already noted on sase-1b1.8.4). Proposed by sase-1b2.20 note #4 (epic sase-1b2).
